ideas.pitch: A captcha system that forces users to solve real-world quantum physics equations or wait for radioactive decay to prove they are human.
ideas.title: QuantumCaptcha
ideas.why_it_could_win: Leverages pure satirical over-engineering with a deadpan pitch deck, perfectly fitting the 'Bad Ideas Only' format where judges look for the most useless tech product.

ideas.pitch: An enterprise-grade cloud platform that intercepts your phone's AirDrop files and automatically prints every single packet out via physical thermal receipt printers.
ideas.title: AirDropShare-To-Printer
ideas.why_it_could_win: Combines chaotic system architecture with physical comedy in the live demo, satisfying the 'worst business model' requirement.

ideas.pitch: A smart fridge monitor that uses high-end computer vision and LLMs to scream insults at you in a Gordon Ramsay voice whenever you look at a vegetable.
ideas.title: AI-Powered-Fridge-Screamer
ideas.why_it_could_win: AI-generated mockups for a completely fabricated problem with an aggressive monetization strategy will stand out during the Shark Tank Q&A.

ideas.pitch: A blockchain-powered Web3 sleep tracker that penalizes you with crypto transaction fees if you wake up before noon, destroying your net worth for productivity.
ideas.title: ProofOfSnooze
ideas.why_it_could_win: Mocks the absurdity of modern Web3 tokenomics and financial incentive structures, appealing to judges with a sarcastic business plan.

ideas.pitch: A completely serverless backend database that stores all user application data inside deeply nested Microsoft Excel macros and VLOOKUP functions.
ideas.title: ExcelAsAService
ideas.why_it_could_win: Presents a truly horrific, nightmarish system architecture that embodies the spirit of over-engineering the worst possible solution.
